result.description: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) for sending and receiving WhatsApp messages, templates and media, and managing business accounts and phone numbers.
result.auth_detail: Bearer access tokens on graph.facebook.com. A direct developer uses a System User token, which can be non-expiring. Tech Providers use a Business Integration System User token, obtained by implementing Embedded Signup (Facebook Login for Business, OAuth-style code exchange). Short-lived user tokens exist for testing only.
result.access_detail: Self-serve for your own business: free Meta developer signup, test phone number and temporary token. To let other businesses connect, the app must be a Tech Provider with Embedded Signup. That needs Meta App Review for the permissions and normally Business Verification. Messaging itself is billed per message (utility, authentication, marketing). I did not confirm the exact review requirements on the fetched pages. They are marked "if applicable" in the docs.
result.api_notes: Cloud API over the Graph API (REST/JSON, versioned, v23.0 or later). It covers messages, media, message templates, phone numbers, WABA management, business profile, webhooks, flows, calling and more. Webhooks are required for inbound messages.
result.blocker: Multi-tenant use needs Tech Provider status and Embedded Signup, with Meta App Review and likely Business Verification. Per-message billing applies. Inbound messages need webhooks. Meta's official MCP is aimed at dev and test setup, not production sending.

evidence.quote: user access tokens expire quickly, so you have to keep generating a new one every few hours.
